meta.notes: Adapted from data/seed/cln_graph.json (CLN / Batten slice, 5 diseases) by scripts/seed-to-graph.ts. Seed edge dates are retrieval dates; curated edges carry their source's date. Keyword and directory matches are marked inferred. Phenotype labels are from HPO (2026-09-01); 57 of 60 seed labels were corrected because the seed paired Monarch's phenotype ids and names out of order. Hand-curated from data/curated/ncl_facts.json (checked 2026-10-03): 7 mechanisms of the missing proteins, 12 gene-mechanism links, and onset and inheritance for 5 diseases; every link quotes its source verbatim in its evidence. The seed's own mechanism is kept: it is the family's definition and links every disease. Sources disagree on the onset of CLN2 and CLN7; the edge evidence says how, and a clinician should confirm. Dropped 9 exact repeats of seed edges. 5 edge ids got a -2/-3 suffix because the seed reused them for different source records. 28 of 40 clinical studies are search hits that matched no disease keyword; they are kept without a disease link. No name in the seed, so labeled by id: PMID:31393684, PMID:31393685.

nodes.label: Removing palmitate from proteins
nodes.description: The enzyme cuts a fatty acid (palmitate) off proteins so the lysosome can break them down.
nodes.source: Zhang et al. 2025, Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis: Concepts, Classification, and Avenues for Therapy (CNS Neuroscience & Therapeutics)

attributes.quote: In the lysosome, PPT1 cleaves the thioester linkage of the fatty acid palmitate‐to‐cysteine residues of palmitoylated proteins (constituents of ceroid), a crucial step for their degradation within lysosomes

nodes.label: Sending new lysosomal enzymes out of the ER
nodes.description: The missing protein sits in the endoplasmic reticulum and helps send newly made lysosomal enzymes on towards the lysosome.
nodes.source: Zhang et al. 2025, Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis: Concepts, Classification, and Avenues for Therapy (CNS Neuroscience & Therapeutics)

attributes.quote: CLN6 and CLN8 are obligate partners for the recruitment of newly synthesized lysosomal enzymes at the ER

nodes.label: Lysosomal membrane protein
nodes.description: The missing protein works in the membrane of the lysosome or the late endosome.
nodes.source: Zhang et al. 2025, Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis: Concepts, Classification, and Avenues for Therapy (CNS Neuroscience & Therapeutics)

attributes.quote: CLN7 is located in lysosomes and endosomes and is considered as an endolysosomal chloride channel

nodes.label: Transport across the lysosomal membrane
nodes.description: The missing protein moves molecules or ions across the lysosomal membrane.
nodes.source: Zhang et al. 2025, Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis: Concepts, Classification, and Avenues for Therapy (CNS Neuroscience & Therapeutics)

attributes.quote: CLN3 is required for the efflux of GPDs from the lysosome

nodes.label: Lysosomal lipofuscin accumulation
nodes.description: Shared process. Not a claim that one therapy treats the other CLNs.

nodes.label: Membrane protein missing
nodes.description: The missing protein sits in a cell membrane, so it cannot pass from one cell to another. A therapy has to reach each cell.
nodes.source: Zhang et al. 2025, Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis: Concepts, Classification, and Avenues for Therapy (CNS Neuroscience & Therapeutics)

attributes.quote: five encoding transmembrane proteins with various subcellular locations ( CLN3 , CLN6 , CLN7/MFSD8, CLN8 , and CLN12 / ATP13A2 )

nodes.label: Trimming small peptides
nodes.description: The enzyme trims three amino acids at a time off small proteins being broken down in the lysosome.
nodes.source: Zhang et al. 2025, Neuronal Ceroid Lipofuscinosis: Concepts, Classification, and Avenues for Therapy (CNS Neuroscience & Therapeutics)

attributes.quote: The mature enzyme cleaves tripeptides from the amino terminus of small polypeptides undergoing degradation in the lysosomes.

nodes.label: Soluble lysosomal enzyme missing
nodes.description: The missing protein is an enzyme that floats inside the lysosome. Cells can take it up from outside (cross-correction), which is why enzyme replacement and gene therapy can also help neighbouring cells.
nodes.source: Cross-species efficacy of enzyme replacement therapy for CLN1 disease in mice and sheep (J Clin Invest 2022)

attributes.quote: These are soluble lysosomal enzymes that can be secreted and taken up by cells via mannose-6-phosphate receptors (MPRs) in a process named “cross-correction”
